title: Which reverse ETL tool fits you?

questions.q: Who should run the sync tool?
questions.hint: Free software still costs hosting and your team's time.

options.label: A vendor runs it for me
options.why: you want a vendor-run service, and Multiwoven and a script are yours to run

options.label: We run it ourselves
options.why: you are happy to deploy and upgrade it (Polytomic offers on-premises only on Enterprise)

options.label: Just a small script
options.why: an engineer can own a short script

questions.q: How many places does the data need to go?

options.label: One or two tools
options.why: with one or two destinations a short script is often cheaper

options.label: A handful of tools
options.why: a dedicated tool starts to pay off as destinations multiply

options.label: Many, owned by marketing or revenue teams
options.why: a script gets heavy as destinations pile up, and Hightouch has no cap on destinations

questions.q: Which vendor do you already pay?

options.label: Fivetran
options.why: one vendor covers loading and sending data back out

options.label: Segment
options.why: you already use Segment, so one vendor covers it

options.label: None of these
options.why: you are free to pick any tool

questions.q: How fresh must the synced data be?

options.label: Hourly or slower is fine
options.why: Hightouch's lower plans run hourly at most, which is fine here

options.label: Every 15 minutes or faster
options.why: Segment's shortest published gap is 15 minutes

questions.q: Can the tool write to your warehouse?
questions.hint: Some tools keep their sync state in your warehouse, so they need write access.

options.label: Yes, that is fine
options.why: Segment, RudderStack and Fivetran Advanced all keep state in your warehouse, so they need write access

options.label: No, read-only access only
options.why: Segment and RudderStack keep sync state in your warehouse; Fivetran Basic keeps it on its side, but it is slower

questions.q: What does your budget look like?

options.label: I want a free start
options.why: RudderStack Free, Hightouch's 2 free active syncs and Multiwoven's free licence are all published

options.label: I want a printed starting price
options.why: Polytomic begins at $500 a month, RudderStack Growth is $265, and Fivetran prints per-MAR rates in a separate table

options.label: I will ask for a quote
options.why: Hightouch self-serve and Segment show no dollar price on the pages we read

hightouch.name: Hightouch
hightouch.summary: A vendor-run tool billed by active syncs, with no cap on destinations or seats.
hightouch.bestWhen: marketing or revenue teams will own the syncs and you need many destinations.
hightouch.watchOut: free and Self-serve plans are limited to hourly syncs, and the self-serve dollar price is not published.

fivetran.name: Fivetran Activations
fivetran.summary: The product Fivetran sells after buying Census, billed by Monthly Active Rows.
fivetran.bestWhen: Fivetran already loads your warehouse and you want one vendor.
fivetran.watchOut: the free plan caps it at 3,500 MAR a month, and the faster Advanced engine needs read and write access to your warehouse.

polytomic.name: Polytomic
polytomic.summary: A vendor-run tool that prints a starting price of $500 a month.
polytomic.bestWhen: you want to know the entry price and need warehouse syncs plus bulk copies in one tool.
polytomic.watchOut: the billing unit is not published, and we found no free tier or free trial.

segment.name: Segment Reverse ETL
segment.summary: Reverse ETL inside Twilio Segment, billed by records sent to each destination.
segment.bestWhen: you already use Segment and want one vendor.
segment.watchOut: it needs read and write access to your warehouse, each destination is counted separately, and no dollar price is shown for Reverse ETL.

rudderstack.name: RudderStack
rudderstack.summary: Event collection with reverse ETL on every plan, and a free tier.
rudderstack.bestWhen: you also want event collection and a free start with a published price after.
rudderstack.watchOut: failed syncs cannot be replayed, a source cannot go to a warehouse destination, and it stores sync state in your warehouse.

multiwoven.name: Multiwoven
multiwoven.summary: The open-source option you run yourself, free under the AGPL-3.0 licence.
multiwoven.bestWhen: you can run software and are happy to host it yourself.
multiwoven.watchOut: you deploy, secure and upgrade it, and the AGPL-3.0 licence needs a read before you build a product on it.

script.name: A short script or iPaaS
script.summary: Custom API code or a general automation tool instead of a dedicated product.
script.bestWhen: you send data to only one or two tools and an engineer can own it.
script.watchOut: every API change, schema change and new destination means more work, and iPaaS tools are not designed to use a warehouse as the source.
